clue.text: Talking about athletics event, what's bad and good

parts.note: the discus is a throwing event in athletics
a sin is a bad deed

explanation.surface: Someone describes a field event and then sorts its bad points from its good ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Discussing a topic means talking it over, so the phrase is a straight synonym in the participle form.

clue.text: Stupid and empty party after party

indicators.note: the emptied word comes after the first party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: emptying the word removes its inner letters, leaving its first and last

explanation.surface: A silly person goes from one bash to another with nothing in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopy is an informal word for dim-witted or slow, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Old poet associated with Marx in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken rather than read, so its sound is taken

parts.note: Spencer is linked with Marks in Marks & Spencer, the British department store chain

explanation.surface: An old poet who had links with Karl Marx, judging by his talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a well-known British high-street store; Marx sounds like Marks, and Spencer sounds like the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Characters starting up keenly get capitalised in this country, briefly

definitions.text: Characters starting up keenly get capitalised in this country, briefly

parts.words: Characters starting up keenly get capitalised in this country, briefly
parts.note: the opening letters of up and keenly, written as capitals, give the short form of the country

explanation.surface: Businesses springing up eagerly obtain funding in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials U and K of 'up keenly' capitalised are UK, the abbreviation; the full name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the country the Telegraph serves, the union of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Band's tour going in one or two directions

indicators.note: the word for tour goes inside the compass letters

parts.note: S and E are two compass directions, south and east
a trip is a journey or tour

explanation.surface: A rock group's tour heading in one direction or another.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a band of colour, a long narrow strip.

clue.text: Main source of oil on earth's disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order, so the clue's three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The world's chief supply of oil has been disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the sea, and the North Sea is a major source of Britain's offshore oil.

clue.text: Surrounded by millions in financial support

indicators.note: the letter for millions is placed in the word for financial support

parts.note: aid is money given as help
M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: A picture of a bailout package worth millions of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, which is to be surrounded by something.

clue.text: Article is penned by man in discomfort

indicators.note: to be penned by is to be enclosed by, so the article and is go inside the word for man

parts.note: a male is a man
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is written by a man who is ill at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease or illness, a vague discomfort.

clue.text: Critical move to the left upset a right-winger

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the words upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: to go is to move
red is the colour of the political left
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A political shift to the left angers a conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks are disparaging ones, critical in a belittling way.

clue.text: Empire replaced king as head of state

indicators.note: the letters of the word for the realm are placed again in a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A historical scene in which an empire swaps its monarch for an elected leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A premier is a prime minister, the leading figure of a state's government.

clue.text: One seeking to profit from illegally acquired stock

definitions.text: One seeking to profit from illegally acquired stock

parts.words: One seeking to profit from illegally acquired stock
parts.note: reads like a fence dealing in stolen shares, but stock here is livestock, and the thief is a cattle thief

explanation.surface: A shady trader trying to cash in on shares obtained by fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, livestock acquired illegally, intending to profit from it.

clue.text: Source of rumours as slander can go nasty about maiden

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the maiden letter
nasty suggests something turned bad, so the three words are jumbled

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden, an over with no runs

explanation.surface: A gossip notices that slander can turn nasty concerning a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads gossip and scandal, so is where rumours come from.

clue.text: Second Dickensian villain's trial for fleecing

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming villain of David Copperfield, and the possessive adds S
a hearing is a trial of a case in court

explanation.surface: The court case of a second-rate Dickens rogue, accused of swindling people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleecing' suggests cheating, Heep's speciality, but it is used literally: shearing the fleece off sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleecing in its literal farm sense is removing the wool coat from a sheep, which is exactly shearing.

clue.text: It's awkward, skilful composer switching ends

indicators.note: the end letters of the two-word phrase swap places with each other

parts.note: deft means skilful
Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: A clever composer finds it clumsy to change direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching ends' swaps the D at the start of DEFTHANDEL with the L at its end. Left-handed can mean awkward or clumsy, as in a left-handed compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-handed has an old sense of clumsy or ambiguous, as in a backhanded, awkward compliment.

clue.text: Announcement of discovery from awful rake attached to multinational group

indicators.note: the rearranged word is joined on after the group's letters

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a group of many nations

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of rake are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful libertine linked to a big international organisation announces a find.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka, Greek for I have found it, is what Archimedes reportedly cried on his discovery.

clue.text: Exhausted down-and-out late to attend

parts.note: the late someone is dead
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A tramp, tired out, turns up late to an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives two definitions plus wordplay: 'Exhausted' (dead beat) and 'down-and-out' (a deadbeat), with DEAD (late) and BE AT (to attend).
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is an idle, penniless loafer, a person who has hit rock bottom.

clue.text: Underwater swimmer straying when beam sinks to bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the beam's letters move to the end of the word

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A diver wandering off course while a shaft of light falls to the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a barbed tail, an animal that swims under the sea.

clue.text: Shoot returning birds showing decorative crests

indicators.note: returning means the word for shoot is read backwards

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
knots are small wading birds

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at birds heading home that have fancy plumage on their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or bow of hair or feathers on top of the head, a crest.

clue.text: Shot from right going in just before end of disorderly cup-tie

indicators.text: going in just before end of
indicators.note: the letter goes in right before the last letter of the jumbled word
disorderly means out of order, so the letters of cup-tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strike from the right wing late in a rowdy cup-tie.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup-tie is a knockout-cup football match; 'Shot' reads as a strike at goal but means a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, and a photograph is a picture.

clue.text: It enables someone without power to take flight

definitions.text: It enables someone without power to take flight

parts.words: It enables someone without power to take flight
parts.note: sounds like an escape route for the powerless, but means an aircraft with no engine

explanation.surface: Something that lets a powerless person run away.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft, so its pilot flies with no motive power.

clue.text: Drop some players produced in a certain mould

parts.note: to drop, as in drop dead, is to die
a cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors are let go, sacked from a show made to a set pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-cast objects are made by forcing molten metal into a mould.

clue.text: Something added up, at this point, in area

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is something added to a letter
here means at this point

explanation.surface: A sum is totalled at this point in a certain region.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field or domain, as in sphere of influence, an area of activity.

clue.text: Connected with pair unfortunately liable to make mistakes

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome suggests things going awry, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone linked with an unlucky couple tends to slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accident-prone describes a person who keeps having mishaps or blunders, prone to error.

clue.text: Within rail network, start from Euston and end in Victoria, or maybe Paddington

indicators.note: the picked letters go within the rail network's letters

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter
the end of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A journey on the railway starting at Euston and ending at Victoria or Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston, Victoria and Paddington are London rail termini, so 'Paddington' looks like a third station; it is Paddington Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru, so he is an example of the animal.

clue.text: One playing with last piece of Waterford glass

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a rummer is a large drinking glass

explanation.surface: Someone toying with the final fragment of a crystal tumbler from Waterford.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterford is an Irish city famous for crystal glassware, which steers the solver towards glass rather than a percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer is a musician who plays, so one playing is a loose description of the performer.

clue.text: Chase out of English party

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: An order to pursue someone fleeing from an English celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' looks like pursue, but in metalwork to chase is to engrave a design.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is decorating metal by cutting or embossing a pattern, a sense of carving designs.

clue.text: Medic joining partnership was in a no-win situation

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
in bridge East and West form a partnership

explanation.surface: A doctor joins a practice and finds it a hopeless position.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players sit as North, South, East and West, and East-West are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: If you drew a game nobody won, so you were in a result with no victory.

clue.text: All its pieces are in one row on it

definitions.text: All its pieces are in one row on it

parts.words: All its pieces are in one row on it
parts.note: the letters of this machine's name can all be typed using only the top row of keys, Q W E R T Y U I O P

explanation.surface: A riddle about an object whose parts are lined up in a single row.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter keyboard has a top row of letter keys, and every letter of the machine's name sits on that row.
